headline: Green claims ban takes effect as EUDR and CSRD rules tighten
summary: The EU's ban on vague green claims is now active, requiring immediate review of consumer marketing. Meanwhile, Germany is finalising its CSRD transposition and proposing severe EUDR penalties. Although your finished imports are currently exempt from CBAM, progress on downstream extensions warrants close monitoring of your products' metal content.

items.title: Ban on vague environmental claims enters into force
items.what: The EU ban on misleading and unsubstantiated environmental claims under the Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive officially took effect on 27 September 2026.
items.meaning: As an EU consumer brand, you must immediately ensure all environmental claims on your power tools, garden equipment, and packaging are fully substantiated.
items.action: Audit current marketing materials and packaging to eliminate generic claims like 'eco-friendly'.

sources.title: EU Rules Against Misleading Environmental Claims to Take Effect on 27 September 2026
Goodbye greenwashing? EU ban on vague claims comes into force

items.title: Member states propose severe penalties for EUDR non-compliance
items.what: Germany and Ireland have drafted strict national penalties for EUDR breaches, including turnover-linked fines and prison sentences. The Commission also established new customs codes.
items.meaning: Even as an importer of finished goods, any wood, rubber, or paper packaging components must comply. National enforcement will be highly punitive.
items.action: Verify EUDR compliance and customs code readiness with your Chinese suppliers.

sources.title: German EUDR draft sets turnover-linked fines and criminal penalties for serious breaches

items.title: Germany nears finalisation of CSRD transposition law
items.what: Germany's SPD announced that negotiations on the national CSRD transposition law are complete, clearing the path for final legislative adoption.
items.meaning: Your company is in scope for FY 2027 reporting. The German national law will soon lock in your specific local compliance obligations.
items.action: Finalise your double materiality assessment and supplier data collection templates.

sources.title: CSRD-Umsetzungsgesetz: SPD sieht Verhandlungen als abgeschlossen

items.title: Digital battery passport services launch ahead of deadlines
items.what: Industry players are launching digital battery passports and certification services, such as TÜV SÜD's new offering, ahead of upcoming EU regulatory deadlines.
items.meaning: Your proprietary battery platform will require digital passports. Early certification options are now emerging to validate compliance.
items.action: Engage your battery suppliers in China to assess data integration readiness.

sources.title: Minespider and Tenways partner on e-bike battery passports ahead of EU regulation
TÜV SÜD launches Digital Battery Passport certification

items.title: CBAM downstream extension discussions advance toward trilogue
items.what: The Q3 CBAM price rose to €82.32/t. Meanwhile, discussions on extending CBAM to downstream finished products containing steel and aluminium are progressing toward trilogue.
items.meaning: You currently import finished goods (exempt), but a downstream extension would directly impact your power tools and garden equipment.
items.action: Monitor downstream extension negotiations and assess product metal content.
